title: Aeterna
titleFull: Aeterna, on-site food waste composter | Phào Design
description: A composting machine that sits in the kitchen itself, turning food waste into compost and into water for the garden growing on the machine.
summary: A composting machine that sits in the kitchen itself, turning food waste into compost and into irrigation for the garden growing on its own rim.
heroAlt: A chef tipping food waste into the Aeterna machine in a restaurant kitchen
cardAlt: The Aeterna composting machine in a university canteen

chapters.heading: The problem
body: Restaurant kitchens and canteens produce food waste every day. It gets collected, then sits waiting for a lorry, and while it waits it smells, leaks and draws insects.
Most existing answers live in a separate area round the back, which means carrying the waste some distance, and nobody who throws something away ever sees where it goes.

chapters.heading: The approach
body: Aeterna deals with waste where the waste appears. It goes in through the opening on top, is ground down, and composts inside the body of the machine.

The waste water, once through a filter membrane, becomes the nutrient solution. It is pumped to an upper reservoir and feeds the garden set into the machine's rim. The rim turns slowly so every pot gets its share.
points: Grinding, composting, filtration and growing in one body
Rotating rim waters each pot evenly
Separate lower drawer for finished compost

chapters.heading: The form
body: The body is one rounded volume, widest at the foot and drawn in at the shoulder, so that standing next to stainless steel it does not read as industrial equipment. A debossed ginkgo pattern runs across the shell, in the same register as the planted rim above it.
The rim is built like a water wheel and sits off-centre on the top, so the green stays visible from across the room.

chapters.heading: Using it
body: A touch panel on the front shows the timer and the running mode. The lid opens to two positions, part way for a quick scrape and fully for cleaning.
Inside are the grinder blades, agitator, water reservoir, vapour vent and a pot system that lifts out so plants can be changed.
Finished compost comes out of a drawer at the foot of the machine, so the top never has to be opened for it.

chapters.heading: Where it goes
body: The machine was visualised in three settings: a restaurant kitchen, a university canteen and a secondary school canteen.

Putting it where people pass is part of the design. With the garden sitting on top of the machine, whoever scrapes a plate sees the result of it straight away. The loop closes where the chef cuts herbs straight from the rim.
